classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish input shifts from output shifts, then map a reference point and the vertical asymptote to draw each image with the specified logarithm on the same axes.

content.prompt: Sketch each graph by translating $y=\ln(x)$. Draw the original curve with a dotted line on the same axes.

answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $x-1$ shifts $(1,0)$ to $(2,0)$ and moves the vertical asymptote from $x=0$ to $x=1$. Draw the translated curve for $x>1$.

spec.description: Dotted original and solid translated logarithm with vertical guide at x=1 and x-intercepts 1 and 2.
spec.mathematics: Original y=ln(x) and image y=ln(x−1), defined to the right of their asymptotes.

answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $x+2$ shifts $(1,0)$ to $(-1,0)$ and moves the vertical asymptote from $x=0$ to $x=-2$. Draw the translated curve for $x>-2$.

spec.description: Left-translated solid logarithm with x-axis labels −2, −1 and 1 and a dashed vertical guide at −2.

answer.worked: Adding $2$ moves $(1,0)$ to $(1,2)$. The domain remains $x>0$, with vertical asymptote $x=0$.

spec.description: Common vertical asymptote on the y-axis and orthogonal dashed guides to the image of (1,0).
spec.mathematics: Dotted y=ln(x) and solid y=ln(x)+2, with guides at (1,2).

answer.worked: Subtracting $1$ moves $(1,0)$ to $(1,-1)$. The domain remains $x>0$, with vertical asymptote $x=0$.

spec.description: Downward translation with a common vertical asymptote and guides to the image of (1,0).
spec.mathematics: Dotted y=ln(x) and solid y=ln(x)−1, with guides at (1,−1).
